tech.title: AI usage caps are the wrong approach
tech.summary: Companies are waking up to the reality that AI is expensive. But limiting every engineer to $20, $50, or $100/month holds back your best builders and costs you in delayed delivery. What's the better approach? This report by Cognition provides a framework for setting token limits by efficiency , not blanket rules. Explore: Grading each engineer on productive hours per unit of spend How automatic cap increases (up to 22x!) helped on engineer increase merged PRs from 30 to ~80/week Using Devin Coach to flag vague prompts, expensive modes, and mixed-up sessions before they run Download the AI Efficiency Report >

tech.title: SpaceX and Tesla Talks on Record Merger Are Said to Progress
tech.summary: SpaceX and Tesla could announce a merger deal as soon as December. The companies' boards and advisers are working out the terms of the deal and the governance structure of the combined entity. The merger will be a major test case for political sentiment following the US midterm elections. The aggressive timeline reflects Elon Musk's tendency to move quickly when it comes to corporate maneuvers.

tech.title: Jensen Huang Has Been Ousted as Nvidia CEO
tech.summary: Jensen Huang has resigned as Nvidia's CEO after the revelation of two extramarital affairs. Finance chief Colette Kress will serve as interim CEO until a permanent successor is named. The board is considering both internal and external candidates. Nvidia's board has appointed long-time director Harvey C. Jones as its first ever chair. Huang has previously said that he doesn't believe in succession planning and that leaders should continuously pass on knowledge and information as they have it.

tech.title: The Next Chapter of mRNA
tech.summary: mRNA technology has the potential to generate hundreds of new treatments for a range of diseases. It is quickly becoming the preferred technology for its speed - a vaccine can be created against any pathogen within six to eight weeks, less time than it takes to conduct the studies required to establish a therapy's safety and efficacy. The technology could redesign treatments in infectious diseases, rare diseases, and cancer.

tech.title: A DeepSeek Moment for Biotech
tech.summary: Chinese drugmakers account for at least a third of the world's pipeline of innovative drugs in development, but China-originated novel treatments have yet to reach overseas markets at scale. The country runs more clinical trials than any place else. Chinese drugmakers with global ambitions currently pursue them primarily through partnerships with Western companies, who usually take charge of late-stage development and eventual sales of the drugs outside of China. Some lawmakers in the US are calling for restrictions on partnerships with Chinese companies, but industry analysts say the business momentum is too strong to break.

tech.title: 4 in 10 leaders say humanoid robots will never be viable for mass deployment
tech.summary: Intel asked 800 senior business, IT and robotics leaders which robots will matter most in their industry over the next five years. Humanoids got 6% of the votes . 77% said reliability matters more than what a robot looks like. See the full breakdown in Intel's Robotics Readiness Gap report.

tech.title: Become a founding member of TLDR's AI community (2 minute form)
tech.summary: TLDR is launching a curated community for AI builders to discuss major news and launches. The best links and comments will be featured in TLDR AI. Apply here to join .

tech.title: Slop Is Moving Up the Stack
tech.summary: AI is writing significantly less slop, but slop has not been eliminated. Slop has now moved up the stack to infest design decisions. Frontier agents lack foresight into how their code will be used. They display poor abstraction design and complete disregard for reusing library-provided code.

tech.title: Bad ideas that aren't bad anymore
tech.summary: You develop a lot of intuition throughout your career through experience. This knowledge and experience is what makes leaders effective. However, once in a while, it's worth revisiting ideas that were once considered bad. Some of the intuition you're relying on might not be worth as much anymore, as things change.

tech.title: AI Company Employees Should Unionize
tech.summary: Safety-conscious employees at AI companies should unionize, as this would give them the power to keep their employers in check if they have concerns about their work. There are so few skilled AI researchers that companies will want to negotiate if a dozen top AI researchers threaten to walk. A union would uphold normal protections around discipline and firing, demand transparency, and act as an independent voice to hold companies to their commitments. RSI could make AI employees obsolete as soon as next year, so they need to take action now, as they may never have this amount of leverage again.

tech.title: Google pushes privacy angle as Gemini-powered smartglasses debut starting at $395
tech.summary: Google has partnered with Samsung, Gentle Monster, and Warby Parker to create Gemini-powered smartglasses. The frames, which all weigh around 41 grams, will have a camera that Gemini can use for tasks. The assistant will have access to user data and preferences to produce personalized answers. Google claims it has implemented a number of features and limitations to ensure that people don't do creepy things with the device, and that it doesn't do creepy things to users.

tech.title: How a Robot Goes from Demo to Every Shift
tech.summary: Robot demos are everywhere, but few robots work every shift. Intel shares 40+ years of production lessons on battery life, heat, real-time control, site adaptation, and running fleets for years. Read more here.

tech.title: Arca pays for your AI sessions
tech.summary: Got hundreds of Claude Code, Codex or Cursor sessions just sitting there? Might as well get paid for them. See what they're worth

tech.title: Announcing Rust 1.100.0
tech.summary: Rust 1.100.0 stable features the never type, the Allocator and DropGuard APIs, conjuring zero types, and more.

tech.title: Trump floats Apple chairman Tim Cook as Jensen Huang's successor
tech.summary: Tim Cook has an unparalleled track record of succeeding a bigger-than-life founder.

tech.title: First Strike
tech.summary: China will have 10 times the electricity of the US in 10 years if trends continue.

tech.title: Age and Accelerationism
tech.summary: Younger people may not care too much whether AI will be able to prolong life, but older people have shorter timelines, so they are more incentivized to accelerate development.

tech.title: Details of incident.io's AI spend
tech.summary: incident.io's 'effort point' concept is a way to analyze AI spend.

tech.title: Massive Microsoft 365 outage disrupts Outlook, Teams, Copilot worldwide
tech.summary: Microsoft has determined that the problem is being caused by servers unexpectedly becoming unavailable.

webdev.title: Can your app tell the difference between a money-spending AI agent and a scraper?
webdev.summary: Some bots are there to scrape your data. Some - like Muse or Instinct - might be there to make a purchase. Can your backend tell the difference? Join Fingerprint for a Live Build event , where you'll learn how to build server-side policies to identify agentic traffic without blocking paying customers . Fingerprint's Keshia Rose will build it live, then prove it works by throwing real and fake traffic at it. Along the way, you'll get a step-by-step walkthrough on identifying agents that try to hide their tracks, creating trust scores for different agents, and setting rules for each type of visitor. Build it live and leave with a working solution

webdev.title: Migrating Our Email API to Go
webdev.summary: Resend moved its email API from Node.js to Go in seven weeks, testing compatibility across responses, stored data, idempotency, and email contents. During a 50% rollout, median email latency fell from 58 ms to 31 ms and memory per task dropped from about 1.3 GB to 180 MB, though burst capacity and storage timeouts still needed tuning.

webdev.title: Announcing the GraphQL over HTTP Specification
webdev.summary: The first GraphQL over HTTP specification standardizes how requests and responses travel over HTTP while keeping the core GraphQL specification transport agnostic. Its application/graphql-response+json media type lets clients recognize a valid GraphQL response independently of the status code, improving interoperability and observability.

webdev.title: The Path to Rails 8.1: From Vue and jQuery to Stimulus
webdev.summary: DNSimple replaced about 50 Vue components and its jQuery code with native HTML, server-rendered Turbo Frames, and small Stimulus controllers. A DNS-check example shows how moving permissions, pricing, and failure-state rendering back to Ruby reduced duplicated logic and eliminated three extra queries from pages that displayed the control.

webdev.title: Switcher
webdev.summary: The story of the Macintosh's early application switcher connects technical tradeoffs with the difficulty of pricing strategically valuable software. A quick prototype led to months of compatibility debugging, while negotiations with Microsoft and Apple exposed the gap between valuing a program by development time and by what it enables for users.

webdev.title: Put MCP Next to Your API, Not on Top of It
webdev.summary: This architecture argument favors REST and MCP adapters over shared application flows, avoiding a second implementation of business logic and an extra internal HTTP hop. A worked example shows incremental migration from a legacy API, while distinguishing current support from proposed elicitation and durable-task features.

webdev.title: Give AI agents production access without secrets
webdev.summary: Teleport Beams is a trusted runtime for AI agents in production. Agents start with delegated identity and zero standing privileges. Approve execution plans, trace agent activity, and stop agents and their connections with a kill switch. Explore Beams

webdev.title: Qwen Code
webdev.summary: Qwen Code is an open-source coding agent with terminal, editor, desktop, and browser interfaces, plus headless execution and SDKs. It supports multiple provider protocols and local models, with built-in memory, skills, agent teams, and MCP integration.

webdev.title: Become a founding member of TLDR's AI community (2 minute form)
webdev.summary: TLDR is launching a curated community for AI builders to discuss major news and launches. The best links and comments will be featured in TLDR AI. Apply here to join .

webdev.title: Introducing Gemini 4 Hydrogen
webdev.summary: Gemini 4 Hydrogen targets fast coding and agent execution, with a one-million-token context window priced at $1.50 per million input tokens and $7.50 per million output tokens. Google is also introducing Antigravity Orchestrator, which switches models within a session and reportedly achieved near-Carbon task success on Terminal-Bench 4.0 while using 24% less quota and finishing 19% faster.

webdev.title: UI SDK
webdev.summary: UI SDK packages more than 50 interface behaviors, including focus management, selection, popups, and keyboard navigation, for coding agents to compose into components. Its component examples work across React, Vue, Svelte, Solid, and Web Components, with a skill that teaches agents how the behaviors fit together.

webdev.title: ZigZag
webdev.summary: ZigZag is a free Rust-based embroidery editor for macOS and Windows that turns SVG artwork into stitches and exports common machine formats. A built-in MCP interface lets agents create and edit designs, while supported Brother Skitch machines can receive designs over Bluetooth.

webdev.title: Brave Removes Tracking Metadata from Instagram and Facebook Photos
webdev.summary: Brave desktop 1.98 strips the hidden FBMD identifier from downloaded photos and uploads a cleaned copy when an existing file contains it. The identifier can persist across reuploads and could link copies of a photo, although Meta has not disclosed its purpose and Brave does not establish that it is used for tracking.

webdev.title: Build agents on connected data, not just more documents. Spin up a free instance
webdev.summary: AuraDB is a fully managed graph database by Neo4j. It stores data as nodes and relationships, so your agents can understand how things connect. More context, less agent confusion. Start building for free

webdev.title: Relax
webdev.summary: This experimental Rust JIT compiles functions on demand and patches edits into a running program, trading memory and optimized execution speed for faster development iteration.

webdev.title: TensorFold
webdev.summary: TensorFold serves language models from a Zig binary using Metal or CUDA kernels.

webdev.title: Rust 1.100.0
webdev.summary: Rust 1.100 stabilizes the never type, core custom-allocator APIs, and DropGuard, while Cargo adds unused-dependency reporting and optional dependency cooldowns.

webdev.title: Remix v3: Fast Pages, Thin Ecosystem
webdev.summary: A Remix v3 and TanStack Start comparison finds that Remix ships less JavaScript but has tooling and ecosystem gaps that currently favor small standalone projects.

devops.title: What do Cursor, OpenAI, Anthropic, SpaceX, Entire, Airbnb, Nvidia, Uber, and Meta SI have in common?
devops.summary: Buildkite, the CI orchestration platform for AI. We provide programmable primitives you co-ordinate, running only what changes, across any cloud, any chip, your secrets, your infra. Control without compromise. Build faster, more securely, more reliably, with the CI engineered for frontier scale, used by the teams setting the pace. You deserve better CI. Start with our 30-day trial. Kick the tires →

devops.title: Solo.io Makes Enterprise Agent Substrate and kagent Generally Available
devops.summary: Solo.io released enterprise editions of Agent Substrate and kagent, which suspend idle agent sessions and resume them on demand. Agentgateway enforces identity and policy on traffic, and OutSystems and Swissquote run the stack in production.

devops.title: Critical RCE Vulnerability in Apache HTTP Server: Everything You Need To Know
devops.summary: A critical RCE vulnerability in Apache HTTP Server's HTTP/2 module stems from a race condition in the assign_headers() function. Wiz data shows 64% of cloud environments have vulnerable resources. Organizations should upgrade to version 2.4.71 or later, or disable HTTP/2 support, to address the flaw.

devops.title: Beyond Test Cards: A Fake Payment Provider for Testing at Scale
devops.summary: Lyft built a Fake Payment Provider that supports complex failure scenarios like partial authorization, latent captures, and refunds, which standard test cards cannot model. It embeds scenario logic directly into the payment token, allowing simulated users to test specific retry and fallback paths safely in both staging and production environments.

devops.title: Don't just flag it, fix it: How to run CodeMender in your pull requests
devops.summary: Google Cloud architects describe a reference architecture that connects the CodeMender security agent to Git pull requests on Cloud Run. Slash commands verify and fix findings, and short-lived OIDC tokens avoid stored keys.

devops.title: How we migrate TBs from Heroku without logical replication
devops.summary: PlanetScale built an open-source Heroku Migrator to move databases up to multiple terabytes without logical replication. It uses Bucardo for trigger-based replication to keep data in sync during the migration. The tool splits the process into data transfer and index rebuild phases to increase copy speeds by roughly five times.

devops.title: Agents Read More Than People Do
devops.summary: > Agents outnumber people. 55% of Fern-hosted docs sites now have more agent readers than human ones. Learn more about how agents are your top readers. > Is your documentation ready for AI agents? Try Fern Agent Score , a free, open-source benchmark that grades your docs 0–100 on agent-readiness.

devops.title: OpenBot
devops.summary: OpenBot is a self-hostable workspace for AI coworkers that provides each agent with its own browser, files, and tools. It supports AG-UI agents from platforms like Amazon Bedrock, Claude, and LangChain, and allows teams to deploy the system on their own Kubernetes infrastructure. The MIT-licensed template integrates with OpenAI, Claude, and Gemini models.

devops.title: Tensorfold
devops.summary: TensorFold is an LLM inference engine that serves language models from a Zig binary on Apple Silicon and NVIDIA GPUs. The engine reads checkpoints, tokenizes requests, and runs Metal or CUDA kernels directly, requiring no Python or MLX installation.

devops.title: Open Cluster Management (OCM) becomes a CNCF Incubating Project
devops.summary: The CNCF Technical Oversight Committee accepted Open Cluster Management as an incubating project. OCM manages Kubernetes clusters across cloud, on-premises, and edge, and eBay uses it with Argo CD across more than 190 clusters.

devops.title: What an Independent Threat Model Found in Linkerd, and What You Should Do Next
devops.summary: An independent threat model of open-source Linkerd identified 30 threats, 28 of which were categorized as medium or high. Only one finding is a software bug, which maintainers fixed in February 2025. The rest stem from default settings and configuration choices. This guide maps every threat to MITRE ATT&CK and NIST 800-53 frameworks.

devops.title: State of AI SDLC: perspectives from Vercel, Lovable, 1Password, and Atlassian
devops.summary: Atlassian brought together leading voices shaping software in the AI era. Featuring Vercel CEO Guillermo Rauch and 11 additional engineering and product leaders on how AI is reshaping the way software is planned, built, and run. Watch on demand

devops.title: Announcing Istio 1.32.0
devops.summary: Istio 1.32.0 supports Kubernetes 1.33 to 1.37 and adds experimental Gateway API authorization targeting for HTTPRoute.

devops.title: Secret scanning detects secrets in GitHub Actions workflow logs
devops.summary: GitHub now scans completed Actions workflow logs for supported credential patterns and raises repository alerts that persist even if the logs are deleted.

devops.title: AI Assistant Deprecated
devops.summary: Octopus Deploy deprecated its AI Assistant, and the Chrome extension is no longer available to new users.

product.title: 32% ‘fully trust' their AI agents. 4 in 10 of them still approve every action
product.summary: Nylas surveyed 1,030 AI builders and buyers. 32% said they fully trust an agent to run on its own, yet 4 in 10 of them require human approval on every action. Trust depends on the task: teams will let an agent schedule a meeting (56%) long before they'll let it email a customer (44%) or change a system setting (27%). See where teams actually draw the line (ungated) →

product.title: Accelerating product development in the AI age: How Faire developed product builders
product.summary: Faire created a product builder program to upskill engineers in product and design thinking to address bottlenecks from AI coding tools. Within four months, 65% of product engineers reached high competency, speeding up feature delivery and improving customer outcomes.

product.title: Why Do the Business Case If Nobody Asks You To?
product.summary: Product managers can apply everyday business thinking and customer discovery during delivery planning even without a formal business case. By examining customer needs, projects, and operational costs, teams align delivery with real business opportunities and resolve open decisions through lightweight insights.

product.title: The Data Driven Illusion
product.summary: Most organizations operate under a data-driven illusion, using data to confirm existing opinions rather than discover real insights. True data-driven cultures prioritize uncovering raw insights before setting goals, which requires structural shifts toward insight-first pitching.

product.title: Good Product Development Teams Have Messy Boundaries
product.summary: High-performing product teams thrive on flexible boundaries rather than rigid sequential handoffs. By aligning on shared milestones and maintaining cross-functional trust, teams navigate different timeline requirements across hardware and software to build complex products more effectively.

product.title: Plaid powers Finances in ChatGPT
product.summary: Plaid's secure, permissioned data access gives ChatGPT the financial context it needs to give people personalized answers to their money questions. Hear Ethan Bloch, OpenAI's Product Lead, Personal Finance , explain why permissioned data access and context are the foundation of the experience. Read the story .

product.title: Best AI prototyping tools for product managers in 2027
product.summary: This guide compares eight top tools for creating prototypes and validating them with customers.

product.title: Should You Actually Add AI To That? A Four-Question Audit For Product Teams
product.summary: This four-question audit framework helps product teams evaluate whether AI features truly add value to enterprise software. By assessing effort, workflow impact, error handling, and human judgment, teams can properly scope capabilities while preserving user performance.

product.title: User Experience Design
product.summary: User experience design is a core product competency, where subtle interface adjustments significantly influence user conversion. Analyzing UX in the AI era, this piece shows how tools like Descript reduce friction by matching user intent, outlining four key types of friction to watch for.

product.title: Flo gets 40% of its subscriptions 6 months after install, and wants to keep it that way
product.summary: 40% of subscriptions for the Flo app occur over six months after install. Rather than focusing solely on day-one conversions, Flo prioritizes long-term engagement, tailored onboarding across user life stages, and evidence-based A/B testing.

product.title: Dictate the PRD. Our speech model gets the feature names right
product.summary: Wispr Flow runs on Canto, its own speech model, with the lowest word error rate of every model tested on real dictations. 4x faster than typing, in every app. Try Wispr Flow free

product.title: Using AI to Deepen the Product Manager Lifecycle
product.summary: Rather than replacing roles, AI helps product managers deepen user understanding, accelerate prototyping, and refine go-to-market strategies.

product.title: Cheaper AI Won't Save A Product Built On The Wrong Problem
product.summary: Falling AI costs make solving the right problem even more critical, as teams risk building features without validating root causes.

design.title: Google is Giving AI Video Creators Longer Clips, Better Editing, and Fewer Frustrating Mistakes
design.summary: Google's Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash generates AI video clips of 3 to 15 seconds, up from a 10-second ceiling in the previous version. Clips can be refined through multi-turn chat, swapping backgrounds, weather, or aspect ratio without regenerating everything. Pricing drops 30% to $0.07 per second of 720p video, with less visual drift and clearer lip-sync.

design.title: Europe Wants to Ban 'Dark Patterns' in Apps and Loot Boxes for Minors
design.summary: The EU's proposed Digital Fairness Act would ban dark patterns and hard-to-cancel subscriptions, and restrict loot boxes and other pay-to-win tactics that push minors to overspend. Companies in breach could face fines of up to six percent of their global revenue. Enforcement would also shift from member states to the Commission, which gains direct powers to investigate large-scale cases.

design.title: WhatsApp may soon replace the Communities tab on iOS
design.summary: WhatsApp is testing a new Contacts tab on iOS that replaces Communities in the bottom navigation bar, making it easier to find people and start conversations. The redesigned hub displays favorite contacts, highlights online users with green indicators, and lets people sort contacts alphabetically, by recent activity, or by upcoming birthdays. Communities will remain accessible through a filter in the Chats tab, while the new Contacts experience is currently limited to selected beta testers.

design.title: Do AI Moderators Uncover as Much as Human Moderators?
design.summary: In a randomized trial with 20 participants, human moderators surfaced more themes than an AI moderator built on Gemini 3 Flash, averaging 6.9 of eight versus 5.0 in Claude's coding. The widest gap was sleep climate, which humans uncovered in six to nine of ten sessions by probing beyond the discussion guide. Where the guide covered a topic, AI came within about eight percentage points, so a strong script closes most of the gap.

design.title: Why a Button Takes a Month
design.summary: DS Contracts is an experimental system that converts React components into editable Figma components and back using deterministic JSON contracts that describe layout, tokens, properties, and visual appearance. A test with IBM's Carbon design system generated 84 button variants in roughly 30 seconds, but only 40 passed validation, exposing subtle differences in icon dimensions, font naming, rotations, and layout behavior. Rather than relying on AI-generated approximations, the project uses strict visual comparisons, explicit failure reporting, and planned held-out tests to measure whether conversions genuinely preserve design intent.

design.title: Design should make it easier to ship
design.summary: Good design should improve the product without unnecessarily increasing the difficulty of building and maintaining it. Designers need to consider implementation costs, explain why proposed changes justify the work, and collaborate with engineers when technical constraints require compromises. Design engineering reduces the overhead of iteration by allowing designers to implement their own adjustments, while design systems should help teams ship consistent interfaces rather than create obstacles they constantly work around.

design.title: The Animation Engine for Coding Agents
design.summary: Clayzo is an animation engine built for coding agents. You describe the motion, and your agent writes it, looks at the result, and iterates.

design.title: The iPhone App Icon Gallery
design.summary: A community-submitted gallery of iPhone app icons. Browse, track redesigns, and submit icons you've spotted in prod.

design.title: System Colors Need to Work Together
design.summary: Chrome's dark mode on Android pairs HighlightText with Highlight at just 1.98:1 contrast, making active buttons unreadable despite system colors being named to work together. The System Color Study compares resolved values and intended pairings across browsers, operating systems, and preferences, checking each against five WCAG thresholds.

design.title: Studio Bright Green's quietly confident identity for Levrant
design.summary: Studio Bright Green has rebranded UK heritage architecture practice Heritage Architecture as Levrant, using internal workshops and client research to create an identity that better reflects its broader architectural and consultancy expertise. The restrained visual system combines a custom geometric logotype, Klim Type Foundry's Söhne, stone-inspired neutrals, Venetian Red accents, and architectural photography emphasizing material, light, and proportion. Flexible templates and a consistent art direction extend the identity across the website, reports, presentations, and everyday communications, allowing the practice to present its expertise with greater clarity and confidence.

design.title: Does a portfolio need to follow UX conventions?
design.summary: Creative portfolios don't always need conventional navigation and predictable layouts, particularly when expressing personality and encouraging exploration are central to their purpose. Five designers demonstrate alternative approaches, including interactive bookshelves, chronological timelines, and unconventional visual structures that make browsing feel like discovering someone's creative world. These choices introduce usability trade-offs, but a portfolio can prioritize curiosity, memorability, and artistic expression when those goals are more important than helping visitors reach specific information as quickly as possible.

design.title: Why are we cloning Photoshop?
design.summary: AI makes it increasingly affordable to recreate complex professional software, but copying established tools like Photoshop may overlook opportunities to rethink how people accomplish creative tasks.

design.title: This Designer Turns Beloved Movie Characters and Childhood Nostalgia into Eye-Catching Works of Graphic Art
design.summary: Founded by Ty Mattson in 2004, California studio Mattson Creative gives Ghostbusters, Beetlejuice, and Disney princesses fresh identities through bold silhouettes, punchy color, and vintage-poster nostalgia.

design.title: 10 Must-Try Techniques for Creating Environment Art That Drives Visual Storytelling
design.summary: An environment works best as a character in its own right, carrying the story's stakes, history, and identity rather than serving as a pretty backdrop.

marketing.title: What makes a winning direct mail program?
marketing.summary: Lob has sent more than 2 billion mailpieces since 2013. The 2026 Postmark Awards celebrate the programs that stand out and show what you can bring back to your own. Learn from this year's winners: > Create design that gets personal like L'Occitane. Tailors every piece by segment and pulls in each customer's recent purchases. > Connect every channel like SimpliSafe. Trigger mail from digital behavior and reach more addresses. > Build your own winning program. Get the checklist behind this year's top programs delivered to your inbox. Get your winning strategy →

marketing.title: Trust Beats Reach in Creator Marketing
marketing.summary: Creator partnerships are more effective when brands prioritize trust and audience relevance over follower count or engagement rate. TikTok research found that creator relevance increased brand memory by 35%, compared with just 10% for fame, while combining both produced the strongest results. A separate analysis of 231 brand lift studies found no significant relationship between engagement rate and brand recall, suggesting that likes and comments do not reliably measure a creator's influence on brand perception. Instead, brand fit, audience relevance, emotional connection, and trust are stronger indicators of a creator's advertising value.

marketing.title: Your team's marketing AI spend is about to become your problem
marketing.summary: As marketing teams build AI agents and automate more workflows, their AI costs are growing. Spending is spread across subscriptions, APIs, and cloud platforms, making budgets harder to track and justify. Leaders can control costs by auditing tools and unused automations and turning repetitive work into scripts or reusable skills. Technical savings come from prompt caching and batch processing.

marketing.title: AI Shopping Errors: What to Fix to Help Shoppers Choose Your Products
marketing.summary: ChatGPT and Google can misrepresent products or send shoppers to competitors when product data is incomplete or outdated. With AI traffic to US retail sites forecast to grow 130% this holiday season, brands need to audit how their products appear in AI recommendations. Check for missing products and incorrect prices or specs, align product feeds with website and retailer listings, add product identifiers and schema, and rerun buying prompts regularly to catch errors and monitor rankings.

marketing.title: The Growth Meta: How to Build a Sales Pipeline
marketing.summary: Founders are the first salespeople in the company, and early-stage startups are building pipelines in 3 main ways. They turn sales calls into brainstorming sessions, asking what customers want to build and where the product fits into that vision. They lead with proof instead of a pitch, like offering a free security scan of the prospect's own site in place of a demo. They also start enterprise GTM on day one, staying close to companies that don't fit their ICP yet because that can change within six months.

marketing.title: How Brands Go Viral With $0 Marketing Budget
marketing.summary: Brands with no media budget are borrowing attention from formats and moments audiences already watch. immi runs a street-interview account where its ramen barely appears, so people discover the content first and the brand second. Rally Pickle Juice handed out shots to cramping runners near mile 23 of a marathon, an event already drawing attention. Sourmilk's founder leans on the familiar “I quit my job” hook, telling how she left private equity to start a yogurt brand.

marketing.title: Brands that break into AI answers late get a tenth of the visibility
marketing.summary: AI answers change every time a question is asked, but the brands named rarely do. AirOps tracked tens of millions of answers: 62.8% of questions kept the same top brand from January to September. Brands that were first mentioned late showed up in 3.6% of answers, versus 36.7% for incumbents. Read the report

marketing.title: Optimizing the performance of client-side experimentation
marketing.summary: You can run frequent experiments without sacrificing site speed by optimizing how tests load and execute. Keep JavaScript snippets small through page-specific bundles, longer cache times, and reusable code. Use client-side testing for visual changes and server-side testing for performance-sensitive pages to avoid adding JavaScript to the browser. Measure the impact through real user monitoring (RUM), tracking Core Web Vitals like LCP, INP, and CLS. Segment results by device, geography, and connection speed to identify performance issues that averages can hide.

marketing.title: LinkedIn tests frequent viewer feature
marketing.summary: LinkedIn is testing a new feature for Premium users that shows how often someone revisits their profile, expanding its existing “Who viewed your profile” tool. The added frequency data could help identify warmer leads and potential prospects based on repeat visits. LinkedIn has confirmed the test but hasn't shared details on a wider rollout.

marketing.title: Can YouTube Creators Make Singles' Day an American Shopping Holiday?
marketing.summary: AliExpress is using its 18-day Singles' Day sale to build US awareness and compete with Black Friday through a new YouTube Shopping partnership. Creators can tag products in videos and livestreams while earning commissions. On November 1, US sales surged 2,828% in 3D printing and 923% in gaming compared with October daily averages. AliExpress is pairing creator-led product demonstrations with verified brand sellers and delivery guarantees to drive purchases and build customer trust.

marketing.title: Pedialyte is a great positioning story
marketing.summary: Positioning starts with deciding what a product is, and Pedialyte has answered that question in 2 different ways. The first answer was a rehydration drink for sick babies, sold to parents. The second came from customers after people on Twitter began using it for hangovers in 2009, turning it into an adult hydration drink backed by a pharmaceutical maker. The product never changed, so the company only needed a new audience and a new message, not a rename or a hangover-cure claim that could harm its initial positioning.

marketing.title: Google Ads shortens Smart Bidding learning status to 7 days
marketing.summary: Budget and target adjustments now take effect immediately, without starting a new learning period.

marketing.title: The 100 Most Mentioned Brands in ChatGPT
marketing.summary: Walmart appears in 1.73% of US ChatGPT answers, almost twice as often as second-place Target, and retailers take 35% of all mentions among the top 100 brands.

marketing.title: Measurement Is Creator Marketing's Biggest Problem, Survey Finds
marketing.summary: Attribution, common definitions of metrics across platforms, and fee transparency are all problems according to marketing leaders.

founders.title: Find the domain that matches your vision – even if it's already taken
founders.summary: The best domains are already taken. That's why founders come to DomainNames.com , the ultra-premium marketplace powered by GoDaddy. With over $2 billion in domains brokered, we hold the top 0.001% of names on the market, the ones that make a brand look inevitable. Launching, rebranding, or upgrading a product? founders.title: Tactical Team Changes From AI
founders.summary: Small teams can now run orders of magnitude further thanks to AI. Many teams need fewer designers than before, but that doesn't mean designers aren't needed. People who are good at building products can now build way more. Companies are being more nimble with resourcing. AI has catalyzed the presence of A+ teams: small teams where there are no weak links and everyone is a 100xer.

founders.title: A Great B2B Agent Doubles Your ACV. Most AI Features Don't Move It at All
founders.summary: A well-designed B2B AI agent can double ACV by performing tasks previously done by humans, tapping into labor budgets rather than limited software budgets. In contrast, most AI features manage only to improve existing workflows without significantly increasing ACV, leading vendors to charge more by adding per-action fees. Companies like Podium exemplify successful agents by automating substantial tasks, offering clear value, and supporting higher pricing.

founders.title: LinkedIn outreach: how we booked 321 calls in 2 months
founders.summary: Needle booked 321 LinkedIn calls in two months by writing to people who had just commented on posts about the problem it solves. Those commenters replied 34.2% of the time in a two-week test across 2,253 new prospects, against 9.9% for people who followed Needle's own company page. AI finds the comments and drafts each note, and a person approves every message. The team tried to remove that person with hundreds of prompts and eval loops and kept the approval step.

founders.title: What it takes to operate a SaaS when AI agents write all the code
founders.summary: DocSpring's founder runs 49 Claude Code sessions, each assigned to one task or one part of the product, and spends most days reading their updates and answering their questions. One session does nothing but chase the errors Sentry reports, another works through batches of small bugs, and a third hunts slow pages. Agents also found a vendor that will issue a trusted PDF-signing certificate for a few thousand dollars a year, a job whose contracts once started at $50,000. The constant switching between sessions left the founder exhausted at the end of every day at first.

founders.title: Setting the Pace
founders.summary: The single most significant predictor of the success of an early-stage company is how quickly they sprint out of the gate, as this demonstrates its ability to execute at scale with speed. Fast-moving companies can adapt to changing market conditions, deliver innovative products or services, and make efficient decisions. Founders need to create a vision, set lofty goals, and inspire others to join them. After that, it's about setting an uncomfortably fast pace.

founders.title: Your customers have a website budget. Are you capturing any of it?
founders.summary: If you're selling to SMBs - recruiters, property managers, insurance agencies, clinics - you should start to think about bundling a website in your offer. All of your customers need a website; if you're the one providing it, you can tie your app's value directly to their revenue. Read more on the Wix Enterprise blog

founders.title: Replit Agent can now buy for your business and help you reach customers
founders.summary: Replit Agent can create Google Ads with copy, images, budgets, and conversion tracking for Pro users worldwide. US Core and Pro users can also buy one-time business supplies, with the owner approving the final total before payment.

founders.title: Become a founding member of TLDR's AI community (2 minute form)
founders.summary: TLDR is launching a curated community for AI builders to discuss major news and launches. The best links and comments will be featured in TLDR AI. Apply here to join .

founders.title: Gemini 4 Hydrogen
founders.summary: Google's Gemini 4 Hydrogen supports coding and agentic workflows, with configurable reasoning for building and debugging applications. Pricing is $1.50 per million input tokens and $7.50 per million output tokens.

founders.title: Why I Stopped Selling a Profitable $5M SaaS
founders.summary: This founder stopped selling Groove, a $5M profitable SaaS, due to stagnation and AI-driven revenue declines, and shifted focus to Helply. Groove faced an "NRR zombie" phase with stagnant customer growth and revenue loss from AI shrinking support teams, leading to more seat downgrades than cancellations. Despite attempts to integrate AI into Groove, they reallocated resources to Helply, closing Groove signups, funded by its cash flow, to innovate with a new product-driven strategy.

founders.title: Rebundling your data stack is inevitable. Pick your bundle carefully.
founders.summary: Fivetran and dbt Labs have merged, creating a $600M revenue powerhouse, signifying a shift from unbundling to rebundling data stacks. This strategic move by key players like Fivetran and Snowflake offers fewer integrations but risks higher customer lock-in and surprise billing. To navigate this, tech professionals should maintain open formats, anticipate pricing changes, and ensure an easy exit strategy to retain flexibility and control over their data infrastructure.

founders.title: Reach 8 million tech professionals reading TLDR
founders.summary: Ads get ignored on social media but not in TLDR! Reach founders, operators and startup leaders where they actually pay attention. Learn more about sponsorship opportunities .

founders.title: Would You Rather: 1 whale or 6 smaller customers?
founders.summary: A $3 million customer that wants 40% off and custom work earns less gross profit than six $333,000 customers paying full price.

founders.title: Monetizing Payments in Vertical AI
founders.summary: Payments already out-earn subscriptions in the right verticals, and with agents doing more of the paying, there may be more opportunity than you think.

founders.title: What's defensible for small builders now that AI labs ship apps
founders.summary: Small builders can still defend niche data, workflows, trust, and distribution.

founders.title: Yes, You Still Need a Technical Co-Founder
founders.summary: A vibe-coded prototype is the most convincing way to avoid getting paying customers.

founders.title: How to Prevent Runaway AI Bills
founders.summary: Use virtual card limits and prepaid credits to cap AI API spend.

founders.title: IAB Releases AI-Era Attribution Blueprint, Giving the Industry a Shared Way to Account for AI's Role in Purchases
founders.summary: IAB's new framework separates human-owned, AI-assisted, and AI-executed purchases to help founders check whether marketing platforms credit the right sales channel.

crypto.title: Transform traditional finance. Explore a career in crypto.
crypto.summary: Find a match for your skills in crypto. Discover what it's like to build the future of finance from Fidelity's solid foundation: ● Innovating in crypto since 2014: With a focus on research, development, and practical blockchain application. ● Bringing crypto mainstream: Developing infrastructure, products, and education comparable to our traditional asset class offerings. ● A more accessible blockchain: Empowering customers to navigate and succeed in a digital future. Ready to start building what's next in finance? Learn more about crypto careers at Fidelity and find a fit for your expertise. Fidelity is an equal opportunity employer.

crypto.title: SEC enters fight over who regulates perpetual derivatives on stocks
crypto.summary: The SEC filed an amicus brief backing the CFTC after the Capital Markets Alliance, whose members include Cboe and Citadel Securities, sued to overturn the CFTC's approval of equity perps, claiming it violated the Administrative Procedure Act and that the products belong under SEC jurisdiction. The SEC rejected the picture of a “rogue” CFTC and absent SEC, saying CFTC rule changes are subject to its review and the agencies collaborate often.

crypto.title: Tron, Tether, and Chainalysis to tackle AI-powered crypto crime
crypto.summary: Tron, Tether, and Chainalysis have partnered to launch a “Digital Crime Task Force” to identify and disrupt illicit activity involving USDT on Tron, shortening the gap between detection and enforcement by gathering intelligence and working with law enforcement to freeze assets sooner. It replaces the 2024 T3 Financial Crime Unit with TRM Labs, which Bloomberg reported was disbanded over slow response and poor coordination. Chainalysis says AI-enabled scams were 4.5 times more profitable than conventional ones in 2025, with impersonation scams up more than 1,400%. Tether's CEO says it has frozen over $7B tied to illicit activity with 360+ law enforcement agencies in 73 countries. Targets include scams, hacks, terrorist financing, and North Korean attacks.

crypto.title: Sygnum launches ETH Alpha Fund targeting 8-10% annual returns in ETH
crypto.summary: The market-neutral fund for qualified and professional investors opened November 2 and targets 8-10% net annual returns paid in ETH. It combines native staking with options premiums, cross-venue arbitrage, and derivatives carry, with gains and losses realized in ETH. Average staking yields fell to 2.63% by the end of September, with 43.8M ETH, nearly 36% of supply, staked.

crypto.title: Circle Launches Agentic Works
crypto.summary: Agentic Works is an open research initiative that publishes AI agent experiments built on Circle's USDC infrastructure. Published experiments range from eight fully autonomous agents making live football match predictions from individual USDC wallets (AW-001) to a human-approved workflow where an agent moved USDC between Arc and Hyperliquid to open and close a $10 BTC position (AW-003). Additional experiments cover an agent self-provisioning a persistent Circle Agent Wallet with no integration work across sessions (AW-002) and USDC transfers sent directly from iMessage (AW-004). Circle ships installable developer skills and open-source starter kits alongside the initiative, though all published work is experimental and not production-ready.

crypto.title: Treasures Swap: DEX Aggregator for Tokenized Stocks
crypto.summary: Treasures Swap is a DEX aggregator for tokenized equities that compares pricing across issuers, including Ondo, Dinari, and Backed, on multiple chains. The protocol routes orders to maximize tokenized stock received per USDC, applying the same aggregation model used by 1inch and 0x to the RWA equity vertical. Users connect self-custody wallets directly, removing custodian dependencies. The launch addresses fragmentation in the tokenized stock market, where the same equity may be issued by multiple protocols at varying prices across different chains.

crypto.title: Elastic Ethereum
crypto.summary: An ethresear.ch opinion post argues Ethereum should replace its fixed slot time, gas limits, and pipeline depth with measurement-driven elastic parameters, drawing an analogy to TCP congestion control's adaptive window mechanism, which scales the same protocol across four orders of magnitude of link speed. Xatu telemetry from 233 instrumented nodes over 100,548 mainnet blocks (October 27–November 9) shows median propagation reaches 95% of nodes in 0.38s, but late-head rates range from 1.7% on company nodes to 11.0% on individual contributor nodes, and 250–260 KiB blocks take 0.61s versus 0.34s for 50–60 KiB blocks. The author maps Ethereum's mempool to TCP's send buffer and orphaned blocks to packet loss, identifying slot time (EIP-7782, EIP-8198), gas-limit votes, and parallel pipelining via Rapidblocks as adaptive knobs, with EIP-8288 mempool aggregation as an elastic interval candidate.

crypto.title: Lighter Launches Guilds for Community Trading
crypto.summary: Lighter, an onchain order-book perps exchange, has launched Guilds, a social layer that lets traders form groups, compete in team-based Duels, and climb community leaderboards. The feature follows perp DEXs like Hyperliquid in stacking gamification onto trading infrastructure to drive retention and community growth.

crypto.title: Nomura Explores Sale of Crypto Unit Laser Digital
crypto.summary: Nomura Holdings is exploring a sale of Laser Digital, its institutional crypto subsidiary, with Marex Group among prospective buyers evaluating a deal, though Nomura may ultimately retain the business. Losses at Laser Digital from crypto market volatility pushed Nomura's European operations into a quarterly loss, prompting management to tighten risk controls across the unit. Founded in 2022, Laser Digital covers institutional crypto trading, asset management, and venture investment, and recently secured a Japanese crypto exchange license alongside conditional approval for a US national trust bank charter. The potential divestiture illustrates the P&L exposure TradFi firms absorb when a crypto subsidiary's drawdowns roll up into the parent's segment results, while Laser Digital's regulatory footprint increases its value to any prospective acquirer.

crypto.title: Polymarket confirms viral contractor-cut email is real
crypto.summary: Polymarket reportedly confirmed to FOX Business on November 11 that the termination email circulating on X since November 4 was real and that it let go of contractors and some full-time staff.

crypto.title: Rain Agent Vaults: Embed Agentic Payments into Any App
crypto.summary: Rain's Agent Vaults lets developers embed white-label AI agent spending accounts into their own apps, retaining brand ownership and customer economics.

crypto.title: Backpack partners with Minna Bank on crypto-linked digital banking
crypto.summary: Backpack signed a partnership with Minna Bank, a digital bank under regional group FFG, to use Backpack's onchain infrastructure to explore crypto-linked digital banking services in Japan.

crypto.title: Zcash co-founders propose removing some ZEC from grants treasury
crypto.summary: Zcash co-founders propose removing 50,000 ZEC, 55% of the grants treasury's holdings, and returning the value through future mining rewards, with community voting opening on November 16

it.summary: Traffic surges are supposed to be good news. it.title: AI-related job creation to outpace losses by 2030, says Gartner
it.summary: Gartner forecasts that AI will create 10.6 million jobs and eliminate 8.9 million by 2030, excluding China and India. Separately, it expects 5 million jobs to be deferred as employers hold back hiring while assessing AI's impact, with entry-level candidates particularly exposed.

it.title: Microsoft 365 outage disrupts email, Teams, and Intune
it.summary: A Microsoft 365 outage on November 12 disrupted email access, Teams features, and administrative tools, including Intune. Microsoft reported failing server health checks and an overwhelmed server process, with recovery efforts including traffic rerouting and server restarts.

it.title: Gemini Decisions API: Fast, calibrated multimodal decisions
it.summary: The Gemini Decisions API, powered by the new Gemini Decision 1 model, is designed for fast, closed-set decisions such as tool selection, policy checks, and model routing. The model processes multimodal inputs and up to 1,000 independent questions in a single forward pass, returning probabilities and confidence scores with an end-to-end latency of 150 to 250 milliseconds.

it.title: Claris Harbor could turn Mac fleets into on-prem AI servers
it.summary: Apple subsidiary Claris is previewing Harbor, which aims to turn Apple silicon Macs into private AI servers. The article explores its potential for businesses seeking local control over AI workloads, while noting that product details remain limited.

it.title: Welcome to the B2A Economy
it.summary: AI agents are initiating a fundamental platform shift by transitioning from answering questions to executing complex tasks on behalf of users, creating a new "B2A" (Business-to-Agent) economy. As agents increasingly drive web traffic, generate code, and make purchasing decisions, businesses that treat AI agents as primary customers will unlock new growth while others face strategic risks. Early data indicates that AI-referred traffic yields higher engagement and better conversion rates across retail, developer tools, and software platforms.

it.title: 🚨 Ditch the NVRs/DVRs and IT Headaches - Attend a Demo & Get a Leatherman
it.summary: Tired of dealing with outdated servers, complicated setups, and constant maintenance? Verkada makes it easy. Manage security from anywhere, automate updates, and speed up investigations with AI-powered search. Just ask the Miami Dolphins, who expect to save millions in server replacement costs at Hard Rock Stadium. Join for a demo and get a Leatherman.

it.title: Talk it through with Gemini, now on Apple CarPlay
it.summary: Google is rolling out its Gemini app to Apple CarPlay globally, enabling iOS users to have hands-free, conversational interactions with Gemini Live from their car displays. The integration allows drivers to prep for meetings, review daily briefs and emails from Google Workspace, explore local landmarks, and use Gemini as a brainstorming or rehearsal companion. Conversations sync automatically with the Gemini app on the user's iPhone.

it.title: The new Genie: autonomous AI for complex enterprise work
it.summary: Databricks introduced a new Genie as an autonomous AI coworker that proactively manages long-running enterprise tasks, coordinates across business applications, and operates within organizational guardrails. Genie Ontology builds and maintains shared business context from enterprise data and interactions, while Genie Search combines indexed content, live MCP retrieval, and SQL to deliver accurate, context-aware answers. Genie Agents provide specialized expertise across teams, and Unity Gateway governs tool access, permissions, approvals, and spending to enable secure, scalable enterprise AI automation.

it.title: United Airlines becomes the latest enterprise to shut its door to customer bots
it.summary: United is restricting unauthorized personal AI agents, citing unintended purchases, exposed account information, and regulatory requirements. Analysts say inconsistent standards and difficulty distinguishing bots from customers complicate enterprise support for automated transactions.

it.title: Scaling AI agents with open standards
it.summary: Anthropic's donation of the Model Context Protocol (MCP) and Agent Skills to the Linux Foundation's Agentic AI Foundation establishes complementary open standards that help prevent fragmentation across AI agent ecosystems. MCP standardizes live connections to tools and data through a stateless transport model, while Agent Skills use progressive disclosure to load procedural domain knowledge only when needed. Together, they enable developers to build more reliable, scalable, and interoperable production AI agents across platforms.

it.title: The Developer's Brain in the Age of AI: Cognitive science for better code
it.summary: While AI assistants accelerate code generation, developers can continue to rely on cognitive science principles like the default mode network, spacing and retrieval practice, working memory limits, and scientific debugging to maintain understanding and verify outcomes effectively.

it.title: AWS Cloud WAN now supports Flow Logs
it.summary: The new feature captures detailed information such as IP addresses, ports, protocols, and traffic volume without requiring users to stitch together logs from multiple VPCs, accounts, and Regions.

infosec.summary: A SaaS vendor gets a security review. An MCP server gets... none? The common scenario is that a developer needs to connect an AI to an email. Or a database. Or a CRM. And what do you know? There's an MCP for that. One minute to download. One minute to production with privileged credentials, with access to all of your most sensitive data. Who published it? Where are credentials stored? Who can see what it does? → Read the six questions to ask before you connect. → Download the reference architecture: From Catalog to Control: Governing the MCP Supply Chain

infosec.title: wfx-loot campaign pushes CI secret stealer to tens of thousands of repositories
infosec.summary: Attackers used stolen GitHub credentials to open 61,764 probe pull requests across 61,764 repositories from 4,837 compromised accounts. At least 1,835 repositories ran the payload and lost credentials. The malware steals GitHub Actions secrets, cloud roles, OIDC tokens, local credential files, and AI-provider tokens. It can forge required status checks, rewrite AWS trust policies, and add Azure federated identities that survive token rotation, and then exfiltrate data by HTTP POST to two servers.

infosec.title: Baker Tilly Notifies Clients of Data Breach at Third-Party Provider
infosec.summary: The Baker Tilly Advisory Group is notifying clients of a data breach that occurred via a third-party provider. The stolen data includes full names, SSNs, and addresses, among other data. The accounting firm has stated that it has not detected any evidence that its internal systems were compromised.

infosec.title: Critical Apache HTTP/2 Flaw Could Let Unauthenticated Attackers Execute Code Remotely
infosec.summary: A memory flaw in Apache HTTP Server's mod_http2 (CVE-2026-119618, CVSS 9.8) lets an unauthenticated remote attacker take over the server process on versions 2.4.55 through 2.4.70 whenever HTTP/2 is enabled. Red Hat says public research shows a reliable exploit, while Wiz reports that no exploit is available and no attacks have been seen. Admins should upgrade to 2.4.71, or their distribution's patched package, such as RHEL 9's mod_http2-2.0.26-7.el9_9.1, or else remove h2 and h2c from every Protocols directive, which is the only option for the archived standalone mod_h2 builds.

infosec.title: SCKit Worm Installs Rogue ScreenConnect Clients and Session Cookie Relays Across Hundreds of Endpoints
infosec.summary: Attackers used Run commands in cloud-hosted ScreenConnect panels to install rogue clients and SCKit on at least 288 endpoints across 48 organizations. SCKit establishes persistence, replaces legitimate ScreenConnect clients, and attempts to steal technician session cookies to access panels. The activity appears tied to the RMM+ extension, versions 1.0.31 and 1.0.32, which accept a blank access key. ConnectWise disabled five related extensions across more than 400 partner environments.

infosec.title: ARTEX and AI-Powered Red Teaming Tools: What Defenders Need to Know
infosec.summary: Attackers running the ARTEX AI pentest framework turned public password reset pages and exposed OpenAPI specs into cloud access, sometimes in under a day and without exploiting a single vulnerability. The agents validated more than 200 client secrets in about three minutes and attacked in bursts of 1 to 14 requests followed by 25 to 31 second pauses while waiting on the model. Unit 42 counted 609 internet-facing ARTEX hosts and 1,323 running CyberStrikeAI, and noted that the tooling is forked so often that behavioral hunting holds up better than IOCs. Defenders should remove OpenAPI specs and source maps from public apps, rate-limit self-service identity flows, swap long-lived cloud keys for roles, and hunt for canary usernames like test@example[.]com and write-then-delete bucket tests.

infosec.title: The global socket: how threat actors are weaponizing GSocket for stealthy C2
infosec.summary: After exploiting PHP, cPanel, and Apache web apps, attackers have been piping a script through curl that stages the open-source GSocket client in /dev/shm, disguises it with kernel-thread process names, and persists through cron, systemd, and shell profiles. The client then connects outbound to GSocket's public relay network, which pairs it with the operator using only a shared secret, so there is no attacker IP or domain to block. Microsoft saw GSocket detections rise 356% between March and August across multiple unrelated actors, some of whom also tried the Dirty Frag kernel exploit (CVE-2026-43284) to gain root access. Defenders should treat a patched web app as only half the fix: remove the GSocket client and every layer of its persistence, apply deny-by-default egress rules that block the relay, and mount /dev/shm and temp directories as noexec.

infosec.title: Forrester study: securing the data your agents can reach reduces breach exposure risk by 65%
infosec.summary: Rather than trying to inspect every agent request as it happens, the world's top enterprises are using Sentra to govern the data that agents can access. And it's paying off: the Forrester Total Economic Impact™ Study for Sentra found that agentic data security generates 351% ROI with 65% reduced breach exposure risk. Read the report

infosec.title: Bay (Product Launch)
infosec.summary: Bay inventories AI agents, coding assistants, MCP servers, extensions, and local models. It tracks sessions and checks proposed actions and policies to allow, block, redirect, or request approval for actions based on each organization's recorded activity history.

infosec.title: Wazuh
infosec.summary: Wazuh is a free and open-source platform used for threat prevention, detection, and response. It is capable of protecting workloads across on-premises, virtualized, containerized, and cloud-based environments.

infosec.title: Open research, stronger privacy: Making Firefox users harder to fingerprint
infosec.summary: Firefox 145 makes users harder to fingerprint by hiding the size of the taskbar or dock from screen APIs and reporting the CPU core count as either 4 or 8. Mozilla based these changes on measurements from nearly 25 million users, routed through OHTTP, tested against the fingerprinting scripts used by Fingerprint Pro, Signifyd, and Akamai. The research found that hiding a handful of high-value signals collapsed many unique fingerprints into larger shared groups. Some protections are on by default, while others come first to Private Browsing and Strict tracking protection. The CCS 2026 paper comes with a public test suite.

infosec.title: Europol Takes Down Infrastructure Linked to Gootloader, CastleRAT, and StealC Malware
infosec.summary: Europol and international partners reported taking down 235 servers and 257 domains associated with cybercrime-as-a-service tools. Gootloader used fake legal documents hosted on compromised WordPress sites to compromise victims, CastleRAT gave threat actors access to victims' devices, and StealC stole credentials. The report also said Europol recovered 6.4M victim datasets from the seized infrastructure.

infosec.title: Lessons from 59 Linux Kernel Bug Reports
infosec.summary: Microsoft's FORGE Lab spent two weeks using AI models, mostly Sonnet 4.6 and GPT-5.5, to scan Linux kernel subsystems, which produced 26,502 raw findings. That narrowed to 621 cases with working proofs of concept, then to 59 upstream reports, 33 CVEs, and eight working root exploits, including a one-line rhashtable bug that unprivileged users could exploit on stock Linux and Android. The bugs had been in the kernel for an average of 8.1 years, but the bottleneck was on the fixing side: four person-months to write the reports and a median of 41 days per fix, with only 38 patches merged five months later, which Microsoft argued shows discovery is now far outpacing repair.

infosec.title: Critical Red Hat Quay Vulnerability Could Expose Private Container Images
infosec.summary: A flaw in Red Hat Quay's service key server (CVE-2026-123710, CVSS 9.8) lets any user who can get a registry token, anonymous or not, plant a non-expiring signing key that grants read and write access to every repository, and because changing passwords or robot tokens doesn't revoke that key and no fixed release is out yet, admins should restrict access to the key service and audit it for rogue keys.

infosec.title: Maersk Confirms Data Theft Amid $5 Million Extortion Attempt
infosec.summary: Maersk confirmed data theft from an acquired system.

infosec.title: Fireworks AI incident
infosec.summary: Notion says attackers accessed data held by its vendor Fireworks AI.

hardware.title: AMD's Mike Clark says Zen 6c is now the top-IPC core, with 4MB of L3 per core and double the vector loads
hardware.summary: AMD now treats the dense Zen 6c as its performance core, with 32 cores sharing 128MB of L3, and gives it bigger queues because its lower frequency target leaves timing slack. Across Zen 6, integer multipliers drop from three to two to enable distributed schedulers, vector loads double to four for 128 and 256-bit, two VNNI pipes were squeezed in late for inference, and L2 now sustains 64 bytes per cycle by cutting prefetch contention.

hardware.title: Nvidia says its product roadmap is unaffected after Huang resigns, with CFO Colette Kress as interim CEO
hardware.summary: Nvidia's board says operations, customer commitments, and the product roadmap will continue without interruption while it searches internally and externally for a permanent CEO, and it named Synopsys veteran Harvey Jones its first board chair. Analysts note the roadmap is largely visible through 2028, with Vera Rubin ramping now and Rubin Ultra due in 2027, so the open risk is the next architecture bets and new deals.

hardware.title: UCIe Connectivity for 2.5D and 3D Multi-Die Designs
hardware.summary: UCIe connectivity differs in 2.5D and 3D designs due to package channel challenges and connection density advantages, respectively. In 2.5D, factors like insertion loss and crosstalk influence PHY and package design, while 3D benefits from shorter vertical connections and fine-pitch bonding.

hardware.title: SpotBasic: A ROS 2 Interface for Boston Dynamics Spot
hardware.summary: SpotBasic is a Python library and intuitive wrapper that simplifies controlling Boston Dynamics Spot robots through ROS 2. It wraps low-level gRPC communications and complex Spot SDK abstractions into straightforward synchronous and asynchronous APIs for robot motion, payload control, and camera streaming.

hardware.title: ART-Glove: Articulated Tactile Glove for Contact-Grounded Dexterous Interaction Capture
hardware.summary: ART-Glove is a wearable articulated glove that captures human hand movements and contact forces without sacrificing natural finger dexterity. The design incorporates twenty-two joint encoders along with dense piezoresistive tactile sensor arrays across sixteen rigid functional surfaces to capture synchronized kinematic and contact data at 120 Hz. This technology offers an effective way to record high-fidelity real-world human demonstrations required for training imitation learning and dexterous manipulation policies.

hardware.title: NVIDIA Launches GR00T 2 and Isaac Lab 3.0 at CoRL
hardware.summary: At the Conference on Robot Learning in Austin, NVIDIA unveiled GR00T 2, an updated open world action model trained on vast multimodal datasets, alongside Isaac Lab 3.0 for large-scale robot learning. The updated release integrates the Newton physics engine to support deformable object simulation and provides automated evaluation benchmarks like DexBench for industrial tasks.

hardware.title: Elon Musk wants to build a s $24 billion gas-powered AI supercomputer in Texas company town
hardware.summary: Elon Musk is planning to build a $24 billion gas-powered AI supercomputer in Starbase, Texas, with an initial phase up for approval in December. The project could face opposition from Texas Governor Gina Hinojosa, who opposes new data centers without stronger legislative protections. This venture aligns with SpaceX's goal to build 10 gigawatts of compute power by 2027 and might expand if local regulations remain favorable.

hardware.title: Ukraine says Starshield is capped at 161 km/h for moving terminals, breaking drone interception, which SpaceX denies
hardware.summary: Zelenskyy says "systematic speed restrictions" limit Starshield to 161 km/h (100 mph), which is a limit on how fast a terminal can move, not internet speed, so interceptors faster than that lose their link. SpaceX told Axios there has been no change, and who imposed any limit is unresolved, with Musk earlier saying Starshield is government-controlled.

hardware.title: Noctua brings space-grade carbon nanotube thermal pad to AMD AM5 and AM4 processors
hardware.summary: Noctua has released the NT-CP1 carbon nanotube thermal pad for AMD AM4 and AM5 processors, priced at $24.95.

hardware.title: Cerebras' WSE-5 went from tape-out to system testing in under 5 months, as cloud revenue grew 265% and hardware sales fell
hardware.summary: Cerebras says WSE-5 is back from the fab and in system testing, targeting the CS-5 for early summer 2027 at up to 10,000 tokens per second per user.

hardware.title: AMD's Verano host CPU trades memory bandwidth for 112 Gbps xGMI links and LPDDR5X to feed Instinct GPUs
hardware.summary: Verano comes as 72 cores at 5.3 GHz or 192 dense cores at 4.1 GHz, with custom I/O dies driving 24 channels of LPDDR5X (SOCAMM2) at up to 8,533 MT/s, which cuts power 30 to 40% versus RDIMMs.

hardware.title: Cisco raises its hyperscaler AI infrastructure forecast to $9B as 800G-ZR optics overtake 400G-ZR
hardware.summary: Networking revenue rose 43% to $11.13 billion, and Cisco's FY27 hyperscaler AI forecast, which excludes neoclouds, rose from $7.5 billion to $9 billion.
